edges.description: A hypoplastic dermal lymphatic network cannot carry lymph from the superficial dermis of the lower limbs to the deep truncal lymphatics.
The structurally abnormal lymphatic network is visualized clinically as tortuous, rerouted tracts on lymphoscintigraphy.
Failure to clear interstitial fluid from the lower limbs produces pedal and below-knee lymphedema.

Hydrocele is reported in a subset of affected males, as in Milroy disease, and is attributed to defective lymphatic drainage; the specific genital lymphatic defect has not been characterized in VEGFC patients.
Transient neonatal hand edema has been reported in one proband, implying that the drainage defect can extend beyond the lower limbs.

edges.description: Lymph stasis predisposes to skin infection in primary lymphedema generally; this edge is extrapolated and has not been documented in VEGFC patients.
Upslanting dysplastic toenails result from chronic edema of the nail bed.
Heterozygous loss of Vegfc reproduces the human genotype and produces cutaneous lymphatic hypoplasia with lymphedema.
edges.limitations: Mouse dermal lymphatic anatomy and the hind-paw distribution of edema differ from human lower-limb lymphedema.

nodes.description: VEGFC is the paracrine factor that drives sprouting, migration and proliferation of lymphatic endothelial cells through VEGFR3. With only one functional VEGFC allele, VEGFR3 signaling in lymphatic endothelium is insufficient for normal lymphatic development, the same pathway that is disrupted by kinase-dead FLT4 variants in Milroy disease.

nodes.description: Heterozygous frameshift, nonsense and splice-site VEGFC variants are all predicted to truncate the protein so that it lacks a complete VEGF homology domain, which is required to activate VEGFR3. The c.571_572insTT protein is stable but poorly secreted. In a zebrafish floorplate overexpression assay the mutant proteins lose the ability to induce vessel sprouting, and co-expression with wild-type VEGFC does not suppress wild-type activity, so the mutant allele acts by loss of function (haploinsufficiency) rather than as a dominant negative. VEGFC is secreted as an inactive precursor that becomes an active VEGFR3 ligand only after proteolytic processing by the ADAMTS3-CCBE1 complex. The biallelic p.Ser65Arg allele, reported in one patient, altered this processing in vitro.
